diagram_math_checks.checks: The polyline has vertices (-1,0),(0,1),(1,0) and horizontal zero pieces outside [-1,1]; filled points at all three vertices agree with the Example and Verification 3.1. Axes increase right/up; the function is even.

Plot coordinate u represents physical x=2pi*u; the displayed vertical coordinate v represents 2pi*f(x). Thus v=(sin(pi*u)/(pi*u))^2, by 1-cos(x)=2sin(x/2)^2. TikZ sin takes degrees, so sin(180*u) is correct. Tick labels at u=+-1,+-2 therefore read x=+-2pi,+-4pi; v=1 is correctly labelled 1/(2pi). The plot avoids division by zero on two separate sampled domains and uses a filled center point. The microscopic omission |u|<0.001 is visually closed by the center marker and is only a plotting device, not a hole in f.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Density signs, zero set and tails.
diagram_math_checks.checks: The squared sine quotient is even and nonnegative. Its nonzero zeros are exactly x=2pi*k for integer k != 0; the origin is excluded from this zero description because its value is continuous and positive. The original Verification 1.1 establishes q=2(1-cos x)/x^2 and q<=4/x^2 in the tails, while 2.1 establishes f=q/(2pi); hence the density tends to zero without compact support. The Remarks explicitly say its lobes extend beyond the finite plot window. A 5001-point independent JS check over u in [-2.5,2.5] gave maximum absolute discrepancy 1.170175067954915e-13 between v/(2pi) and the stated density, nonnegative samples, and the four displayed zeros within 1.52e-33 in scaled coordinates.

The local characteristic-function Definition uses exp(+itx). Verification 3.1 proves phi_f=tau; the local inversion corollary uses exp(-itx)/(2pi). Since tau has compact support and is integrable, the displayed inverse convention matches that supplier. The entire original Verification 1.1--3.1 is unchanged and supplies normalization/identity without invoking the figure.
